strengths: The paper addresses an important NLP data problem at substantial multilingual scale. Separating document removal from character removal usefully exposes how Wikipedia article counts can overstate available training material.

The qualitative examples demonstrate real contamination, placeholder articles, and repetition. Correlations with independently estimated bot prevalence support the interpretation that deduplication captures substantial templatic content.

The downstream evaluation covers 50 monolingual Wikipedias, language adaptation, multilingual pretraining, and several tasks. Some practical results are encouraging: Cebuano SIB200 accuracy increases from 0.39 to 0.51, while aggregate monolingual NER performance is preserved. Reporting regressions such as Acehnese is also valuable.
The linked open-source toolkit, training hyperparameters, per-language results, and five-run reporting for several experiments provide a useful foundation for reuse.
weaknesses: The central interpretation of filtering rates as quality measurements lacks sufficient independent validation. Appendix A explicitly removes foreign-script named entities and references, while templatic articles can contain distinct, correct facts. No systematic assessment by proficient speakers measures erroneous removals or quality problems remaining after filtering. Consequently, removing 29.36% of documents does not establish that this proportion is low quality. The four clusters characterize filtering susceptibility; their interpretation as general quality tiers remains unproven. The DEPTH+ correlation of 0.31 provides only limited corroboration.

A major downstream comparison is uninformative because of floor performance. In Table 14, both multilingual models average 0.25 on four-choice BELEBELE, with even English scoring 0.25–0.26. Similarity around chance cannot establish preservation of useful capabilities. XNLI instead declines from 0.44 to 0.43 on average. Tables 12–14 provide no run variability, and treating differences within five percentage points as negligible does not establish equivalence. The multilingual conclusions need an evaluation that performs meaningfully above chance and appropriate uncertainty estimates.

The controls do not isolate the proposed quality explanation. Appendix C trains separate tokenizers for raw and filtered data, while epoch-based monolingual pretraining and adaptation change training exposure when data is removed. The random baseline matches article counts rather than token counts, which matters when deduplication preferentially removes short articles. These comparisons assess composite training pipelines, but cannot confidently attribute differences to removed content being low quality. Controlled comparisons and individual-filter ablations would strengthen that attribution.

Important details needed to reproduce the central audit are unspecified: the Wikipedia snapshot date and extraction procedure, MinHash shingle construction and LSH configuration, and the clustering initialization and manual selection procedure. The code link and hyperparameter tables help, but the manuscript does not adequately identify the data and configuration underlying its exact removal statistics and taxonomy.

Several reporting inconsistencies require correction. Section 4.1 identifies Twi among lower-tier Wikipedias, whereas Tables 7 and 15 place it in Tier 1. In Table 11, the displayed Tier 4 rows yield baseline/raw/filtered averages of approximately 0.63/0.60/0.62, rather than the reported 0.59/0.66/0.66. These errors further reduce confidence in the tier-level interpretation.
